newsitem.title: UK: N.Sea spreads end steady after choppy ride.
newsitem.headline: N.Sea spreads end steady after choppy ride.

text.p: North Sea crude differentials had a choppy ride on Monday but ended on a steady note as forecast cold weather drove oil futures higher and saw Brent paper strengthening over the afternoon, traders said.
"Everything (paper spreads and contracts for difference) eased on the early weakness in dated Brent, but the market turned higher again in the afternoon as paper shot up,' one trader said.
A cargo of Dated Brent loading on Dec 27-29 was sold in early business at Jan Brent -20 cents, 20 cents below the previous deal last Thursday.
Bu the despite an overhang of December cargoes the market improved slightly over the afternoon with trade for the same dates at Jan Brent -15 cents.
The Jan/Feb spread, having traded up to +50 cents early on, slid back to +41/42 but had firmed to trade around +47 cents in late business.
January North Sea crude was offered into a market struggling to absorb end-December liftings at cheaper prices, traders said.
Two Forties cargoes, loading on Dec 26-28 and Dec 28-30 were on offer again on Monday at Dated Brent +35 without receiving bids.
Other grades still available in December included Oseberg and Statfjord, dealers said.
A seller of an early-January Statfjord said he was looking for Dated Brent +35 cents, despite last week's trade at +18.
"It might be too aggressive, but we are testing that on our customers," he said.
On the day that first Iraqi crude exports began loading in Turkey and the Gulf, Mediterranean traders said differentials for Russian Urals were set to come under further pressure.
Urals was notionally pegged around Dated Brent -30/-40 but sellers were reluctant to show numbers with bidders scarce.
